newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TKACHUK SCORES FOUR GOALS AS COYOTES BEAT BLACKHAWKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TKACHUK SCORES FOUR GOALS AS COYOTES BEAT BLACKHAWKS.

text.p: Keith Tkachuk recorded his second four-goal game and Nikolai Khabibulin made 40 saves as the Phoenix Coyotes beat the Chicago Blackhawks 4-2 Thursday.

Tkachuk's third goal of the game, a power-play tally at 10:23 of the third period, snapped a 2-2 tie. Mike Stapleton won a draw in the Chicago zone back to Oleg Tverdovsky at the right point. Tkachuk deflected Tverdovsky's low shot over goaltender Chris Terreri for his 45th goal of the season.

Tkachuk capped the scoring with 21 seconds remaining with an empty-net goal. Teammate Jeremy Roenick had the puck at centre ice and unselfishly gave it up to Tkachuk, who scored from the neutral zone.

"With Tkachuk closing in on 50 and a chance for a four-goal night, I'll give it to him," Roenick said. "Tonight was a big game and he got some big goals for us. I also don't think you can say enough about Nikky's play. When your goalie faces 20 shots in the first and you come out with a 2-1 lead, that tells you something."
Roenick and Craig Janney each had two assists for Phoenix, which is 6-2-1 in its last nine games. The Coyotes moved into a fourth-place tie with Edmonton in the Western Conference.
Phoenix won four of the five meetings this season, winning all three games in Chicago. Tkachuk had six goals in the five games.

"It's just a challenge, they're a good hockey team with some great players," Tkachuk said of Phoenix's success in Chicago. "Every time you come in here you want to do the best you can and this time of year you have to win every game.
"It's two tough teams battling for a playoff spot, we're neck-and-neck with each other. Obviously, there is a lot of pride on our team with Roenick having played here."
Alexei Zhamnov and Keith Carney tallied for Chicago, which is 2-2-2 in its last six. The Blackhawks remained ninth in the West but dropped two points behind eighth-place Calgary.

In Pittsburgh, Joe Mullen scored twice and Stu Barnes added a goal and an assist as the Penguins won consecutive games for the first time in over a month with a 6-3 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs.
Mullen, who became first American-born player in the NHL to score 500 career goals a week earlier, recorded his first two-goal game since the 1994-95 season.
Patrick Lalime made 37 saves and improved to 20-8-2 as Pittsburgh climbed into a tie with the New York Rangers for fifth place in the Eastern Conference.
Steve Sullivan had a goal and an assist for the Maple Leafs, who fell to 1-3-4 in their last eight games and 1-5-1 in their last six trips to Pittsburgh.
In Ottawa, Jody Hull scored the tying goal 1:40 into the third period, lifting the Florida Panthers into a 2-2 tie with the Senators.
Florida is 8-0-1 when Hull scores.
Steve Washburn also tallied for Florida, which is 3-1-2 in its last six games. The Panthers moved six points ahead of the Rangers and Penguins in the Eastern Conference.
Sergei Zholtok and Bruce Gardiner had goals for the Senators, who are 2-1-2 in their last five games.
In St Louis, Grant Fuhr made 28 saves and Pierre Turgeon had two goals and an assist to lead the Blues to a 4-1 victory over the slumping Hartford Whalers.

Robert Petrovicky and Al MacInnis scored the other St Louis goals as the Blues won for just the third time (3-6-3) in their last 12 games and moved into a tie with the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim for sixth place in the Western Conference.
Keith Primeau scored the only goal for the Whalers, who have lost four straight games and remained tied with the Washington Capitals for the eighth and final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.

In Vancouver, Viktor Kozlov's unassisted, power-play goal 2:40 into the third period snapped a tie and Kelly Hrudey stopped 30 shots as the San Jose Sharks ended a five-game losing streak with a 2-1 victory over the reeling Canucks.

Marty McSorley tallied in the first period for San Jose, which won for just the third time in 13 games (3-9-1). The Sharks are all but eliminated from the playoffs, trailing the final spot by 15 points with 11 games left.

Hrudey made two stellar stops in the third period to preserve the one-goal lead. He gloved Alexander Mogilny's wrist shot with 8:42 left and smothered the rebound of Adrian Aucoin's point shot with 35 second to play.
Martin Gelinas scored for Vancouver, which dropped to 1-7-2 in its last 10 contests.
